claims.text: Increasing the Cantor-alloy composition to CrMnFeCoNi1.2 stabilizes the FCC phase.
The as-cast CrMnFeCoNi alloy has a coarse dendritic microstructure.
The as-cast CrMnFeCoNi alloy has limited ductility.
The as-cast CrMnFeCoNi alloy is a single-phase FCC solid solution at room temperature.
Cold rolling to 90% reduction produces massive dislocation density and grain fragmentation.
Severe plastic deformation refines CrMnFeCoNi grains below 50 nm through dynamic recrystallization and grain subdivision.
Annealing at 200°C for 30 minutes can trigger B2 ordering or spinodal-like decomposition.
The 200°C anneal avoids grain growth and TCP-phase precipitation.
The processed alloy will contain a coherent B2 ordered phase within a supersaturated FCC matrix.
High configurational entropy and Mn-Ni atomic-size mismatch stabilize the B2 phase.
Negative Ni-Fe or Ni-Co mixing enthalpy drives low-temperature B2 ordering.
Nanoscale B2 domains contribute to hardness by impeding dislocation motion.
B2 domains suppress grain coarsening through Zener pinning.
The processed material will have a yield strength above 1.2 GPa.
The processed material will have a hardness above 400 HV.
Suppressing TCP phases and introducing FCC-B2 interfaces will improve ductility relative to the cast state.
As-cast single-phase FCC Cantor alloy typically has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 200-300 MPa.
Annealing above 400°C destabilizes the proposed nanocrystalline dual-phase structure by causing grain growth and TCP precipitation.
Reducing the Ni stoichiometric coefficient below 1.0 favors BCC formation or sigma-phase precipitation.
The proposed B2 phase dissolves after annealing for more than 10 hours at 300°C.

contradictions.description: The initial state is characterized as having limited ductility, whereas the baseline assigns it approximately 40-50% ductility, which is substantial tensile ductility unless a different ductility metric or comparison standard is specified.

B2 stabilization is attributed to Mn-Ni atomic-size mismatch in the structural mediator, but the mechanism instead attributes ordering to Ni-Fe or Ni-Co mixing enthalpy; the controlling chemical interaction is not consistently identified.
